On a mobile-sized rendering, the central left-facing profile figure, large feathered headdress, mouth-scroll/curving form, outstretched arm, upper geometric band, and repeated lower side forms remain distinguishable. Fine incised lines are necessarily less detailed at this smallest rendition, but this is normal downscaling rather than destructive blur. The original fresco's worn, mottled, cracked, and abraded surface remains visible and should not be mistaken for encoding damage. I see no blocking, ringing halos, banding, stretching, aspect-ratio distortion, or anomalous resampling artifacts. Verdict: vision_mobile_readable=true; artifacts=false; ocr_exact_match=N/A.

768 WebP: The profile figure and surrounding ritual forms are clearly readable at mobile scale, with the face, headdress feathers, curved scroll, necklace, hand, upper border, and flanking repeated shapes retaining coherent edges and tonal separation. Surface wear belongs to the historic wall fragment. No visible block artifacts, ringing, posterization/banding, geometric distortion, stretching, or scaling damage is present. Verdict: vision_mobile_readable=true; artifacts=false; ocr_exact_match=N/A.

Verdict: vision_mobile_readable=true; artifacts=false; ocr_exact_match=N/A.
